title: The Heir
mood: On Planet Oro the heir may have no friends and no feelings. So she builds herself a way out.

hero.alt: A dark, towering hall of pillars and violet windows, with one small figure standing in a circle of light on the floor.

segs.t: The bolt slid across on the outside of the door. Ruby, a small girl on a stool too tall for her, listened to the boots go away.
The schoolroom was white. It held a desk, a slate and one window too high to reach. The window did not open. Through the glass, the sky of Oro was violet.
She pulled the slate from under her lesson sheets. In the margin she had drawn her tutor, with a beard so long that a little man had to carry it.
“Okay, nobody’s around. Hehe... oh! ...Ahem.”
The tutor stood in the open door. She had not heard the bolt. Ruby made her face go blank, as she had practiced since she could walk.

media.alt: Ruby as a small girl, dark hair over one eye, hugging a pink doll.

segs.t: He wiped the margin clean. “The lesson, Heir. How did everything begin?”
“With a single burst of chaos,” said Ruby. “Balance keeps everything in order now. The books call Balance the Will of the Cosmos.”
“And the worlds?”
“Some grow a will of their own as they age. Even far ones, like Dawnbreak.” She knew that name and nothing else about it. “Oro’s will is Balance too.”
“And the Enders?”
“Long ago Oro fought a terrible war with them. Now nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order. That is why the Enders never came back.”
“That includes the heir,” said the tutor.
“Yes.”
Behind him, a dark ship with a cyan light crossed the window. Ruby watched it until it left the glass.

media.alt: A dark ship with cyan lights crosses a violet sky above the towers of Oro.

segs.t: The summons came the next morning.

The Council hall was dark and very tall. The Council was where Oro’s rulers agreed their orders. Her father led the Decisionmakers, who gave them. Ruby was the heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro, and she stood alone in a circle of light on the floor. He stood outside it.
Heirs could have no friends and no feelings. She had been told so since before she could read. In the schoolroom she had broken the second rule, and now tears ran down her face.
“I am told you laughed in a lesson. Alone.” He did not raise his voice. “Oro has gone unopposed for thousands of years. Its rulers do not bend. You must be strong and unyielding.”
His boot came down on her tears.
“You cannot allow yourself to be so weak. Do not disappoint me, Ruby.”

blocks.caption: Ruby’s father, who leads the Decisionmakers of Oro.

media.alt: Ruby's father, the Decisionmaker: a tall man in a dark coat with a fur collar and a long cape.

segs.t: “...Yes, Father.”
In the corridor she tried the words aloud.
“But I have a plan...”
She had no plan yet. She said it again anyway.
The Laboratory, years later.
One wall of the Laboratory was glass, with only stars behind it. Along the other wall, in rows of cradles, lay the androids of Project “Angel.” Androids were machines built like people.

These were the Council’s androids, all the same girl, with folded animal ears. When woken, their eyes glowed magenta. The soldiers called them Cosmic Reapers. They did what they were told and nothing else.

blocks.caption: The Council’s androids of Project Angel.

media.alt: Rows of identical androids with animal ears and glowing magenta eyes stand in the dark.

segs.t: The Council’s engineers had taught Ruby to program. Now a courier brought the Council’s order. The Balance Keepers, Oro’s special forces, went from planet to planet to keep things in “balance.” They wanted a blade sharper than any they had. The heir would build it.
She built on a Project Angel body and wrote the mind herself, piece by piece. The Council’s checkers read what ran. They never read what slept.
So I can hide something in her,
thought Ruby.
My way out of here.

media.alt: An android girl with pink hair sleeps upright in a cradle of cables, surrounded by glowing screens.

segs.t: Under the walking routines she tucked a few lines nobody had asked for. She put a lock on them that opened to her hand alone.

Every Project Angel body carried a sealed plate between the shoulder blades. It was the size of her palm, with the Council’s seal burned in and one small light, dark. She asked the console to unlock it.
“That part belongs to the Council.”
Three tries got the same answer. Ruby never learned what the plate did, and built around it.
On the last night SUCCESS came up green. Ruby pressed the key, and the cradle let go of its cables. Every other android woke magenta. Hers opened blue.

media.alt: SUCCESS lights up on a screen, a hand presses the key, and the android in the cradle opens bright blue eyes.

segs.t: “From now on, I call you Angela.”
“Yes, I’m Angela!”
The smile was so bright that Ruby looked at the floor. Without moving her lips, she said it to herself.

media.alt: Angela, just woken, with pink hair, white ear pieces and blue eyes, smiling brightly.

segs.t: “You belong to me, and no one else.”
